source_title: PG&E Corporation Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results; On Track to Deliver Solid 2026; Reaffirms 2026 and 2027 Guidance - PR Newswire
source_excerpt:
OAKLAND, Calif. , Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- PG&E Corporation (NYSE: PCG ) is on track to deliver solid financial results in 2026. Progress includes:
GAAP earnings were $0.34 and $1.06 per share for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, respectively, compared to $0.37 and $0.89 per share for the same periods in 2025.
Non-GAAP core earnings were $0.41 and $1.24 per share for the third quarter and first nine months of 2026, compared to $0.50 and $1.14 per share for the same periods in 2025.
Full year 2026 and 2027 non-GAAP core EPS guidance reaffirmed at $1.64 to $1.66 per share and $1.78 to $1.82 per share, respectively. 1
On track to meet 2-4% non-fuel operating and maintenance (O&M) cost reduction target.
Implementing previously announced $2 billion reduction to 2027 capital plan.
Strategic review advancing with the goal of becoming a financially strong, investment-grade company.
"Our PG&E team continues to make meaningful progress delivering safe, affordable, reliable, and clean energy to our customers. While we still believe California needs a durable wildfire liability framework that delivers for customers and investors, safety remains our foundation as we strengthen and build resilient energy infrastructure to support our state's growth," said PG&E Corporation CEO Patti Poppe.
Operational progress during the third quarter of 2026 continued to focus on delivering safe, reliable, affordable, and clean energy to customers. Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E or the Utility):
Filed a 5,000-mile undergrounding plan with California regulators designed to reduce wildfire risk by 98% and outages by 90% on lines moved underground, which is expected to deliver an estimated $117 billion in long-term benefits.
Connected over 4,240 electric customers and 3,000 EV charging ports to the grid.
Launched a first-of-its-kind virtual power plant demonstration with Google and Rewiring America to improve reliability and affordability for customers, targeting over 20,000 new and existing customer energy devices and 12 megawatts of distributed energy resources by 2028.
Delivered nearly $15 million in energy bill assistance to more than 46,000 low- and moderate-income customers.
Energized 174 megawatts of new data center projects since 2024. With appropriate pricing, every one gigawatt of new data center load could help customers save 1% or more on their monthly electric bill.
PG&E Corporation is reaffirming its full year 2026 and 2027 non-GAAP core earnings guidance range of $1.64 to $1.66 per share and $1.78 to $1.82 per share, respectively. Factors expected to drive non-GAAP core earnings in 2026 and 2027 include return on customer capital investment and costs related to unrecoverable net interest expense and other earnings factors, including allowance for funds used during construction, incentive revenues, tax benefits, and cost savings, net of below-the-line costs.
PG&E Corporation uses "non-GAAP core earnings," which is a non-GAAP financial measure that excludes non-core items, in order to provide a measure that allows investors to compare the underlying financial performance of the business from one period to another, exclusive of non-core items. See the accompanying tables for a reconciliation of consolidated income available for common shareholders to non-GAAP core earnings (including non-GAAP core EPS).
PG&E Corporation recorded third-quarter 2026 income available for common shareholders of $749 million, and $0.34 per diluted share, as reported in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). This compares with income available for common shareholders of $823 million, and $0.37 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025.
The decrease in GAAP earnings was primarily driven by lower CPUC return on equity in effect during 2026 as compared to 2025, the one-time catch-up impacts of the tax methodology change implemented in 2025, and increased Wildfire Fund expense, partially offset by increased customer capital investment due to the earnings on higher rate base and net O&M savings.
PG&E Corporation's non-GAAP core earnings were $928 million, and $0.41 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $1,142 million, and $0.50 per diluted share, for the third quarter of 2025.
The decrease in Non-GAAP core earnings was driven by similar factors to our GAAP earnings except for Wildfire Fund expense.
Non-core items, which management does not consider representative of ongoing earnings, totaled $156 million after tax, and $0.07 per share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared with $295 million after tax, and $0.13 per share, for the third quarter of 2025.

Non-GAAP Core Earnings and Non-GAAP Core EPS
"Non-GAAP core earnings" and "Non-GAAP core EPS," also referred to as "non-GAAP core earnings per share," are non-GAAP financial measures. Non-GAAP core earnings is calculated as income available for common shareholders, diluted, less non-core items. "Non-core items" include items that management does not consider representative of ongoing earnings and affect comparability of financial results between periods, consisting of the items listed above. Non-GAAP core EPS is calculated as non-GAAP core earnings divided by common shares outstanding on a diluted basis.
PG&E Corporation discloses historical financial results and provides guidance based on "non-GAAP core earnings" and "non-GAAP core EPS" in order to provide measures that allow investors to compare the underlying financial performance of the business from one period to another, exclusive of non-core items. PG&E Corporation and the Utility use non-GAAP core earnings and non-GAAP core EPS to understand and compare operating results across reporting periods for various purposes, including internal budgeting and forecasting, short- and long-term operating planning, and employee incentive compensation. PG&E Corporation and the Utility believe that non-GAAP core earnings and non-GAAP core EPS provide additional insight into the underlying trends of the business, allowing for a better comparison against historical results and expectations for future performance.
Non-GAAP core earnings and non-GAAP core EPS are not substitutes or alternatives for GAAP measures such as consolidated income available for common shareholders and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures used by other companies.
